authority.legal_name: ACTV (Azienda del Consorzio Trasporti Veneziano), the AVM-group public-transport operator for the City of Venice
authority.geography_type: a shallow tidal lagoon of channels, islands and historic canals
authority.home_waters_label: the Venetian Lagoon and the Grand Canal

mandate.summary: ACTV, part of the AVM group owned by the City of Venice, runs the vaporetto — the densest waterborne public-transit network on earth. More than a hundred floating stops link the Grand Canal, the Giudecca canal and the lagoon islands of Murano, Burano, Torcello and the Lido, carrying tens of millions of resident and visitor journeys a year on water that has no roads at all.
current_priorities: Run the lagoon-wide vaporetto network — the Grand Canal spine, the Giudecca and lagoon-island lines
Electrify and hybridise the fleet — ACTV's electric and hybrid vaporetto program
Protect the city from motondoso (wake erosion) — low-wake vessels and strict speed limits that preserve the foundations and banks
Sustain everyday access for residents while serving more than 20 million visitors a year

policy_targets.vision: ACTV / AVM fleet electrification & hybrid program; EU and Italian clean-transport and lagoon-protection goals
policy_targets.decarb_note: ACTV and the AVM group are electrifying and hybridising the vaporetto fleet — introducing electric and hybrid vessels to cut emissions and motondoso in the most wake-sensitive city in the world.
policy_targets.relevance: Navier is the zero-emission, software-defined passenger-only foiling layer above the vaporetto network — quiet, low-wake hops across the open lagoon to Murano, Burano, Torcello and the Lido that complement ACTV's electrification, with conventional low-speed handling in the wake-protected Grand Canal and inner canals where foiling is never used.

precedent.headline: Venice's vaporetto is the densest waterborne public-transit network on earth — 100+ floating stops across the lagoon — and ACTV is already electrifying the fleet.
precedent.network: Lines run the Grand Canal (Piazzale Roma – Ferrovia – Rialto – San Marco), the Giudecca and Zattere, out to San Giorgio, the Lido, Murano, Burano and Torcello, and along the lagoon edges.
precedent.note: Public ferry service is core transport infrastructure here, not a novelty. Navier adds a fast passenger-only foiling layer on the busy corridors.

interpretation_for_navier: Navier is the zero-emission, software-defined passenger-only foiling layer above the vaporetto network — quiet, low-wake hops across the open lagoon to Murano, Burano, Torcello and the Lido that complement ACTV's electrification, with conventional low-speed handling in the wake-protected Grand Canal and inner canals where foiling is never used.

domestic_network.note: Candidate boarding points with APPROXIMATE anchor coordinates [lng, lat] for Grok to snap to real piers/terminals during seal. Coordinates are anchors, not sealed geometry. Core mirrors the authority's live public stops; new/committed/study stops are flagged.

domestic_pairs.rationale: Fondamente Nove to Murano across the open northern lagoon — the busiest island crossing, ideal for a quiet low-wake foiling hop.
Murano to Burano across the lagoon — the long island run a fast, quiet boat transforms.
Burano to Torcello — the short hop to the lagoon's oldest island.
San Zaccaria to the Lido across the San Marco basin — the city-to-beach crossing.
Fondamente Nove direct to Burano across the northern lagoon — a fast quiet run on open water.
Tronchetto to the Lido around the city — a car-terminal-to-island link on the lagoon edge.
San Marco to San Giorgio Maggiore across the basin — the short island hop with the city's most famous view.
The Lido to Sant'Elena across the basin edge — an island-to-east-Venice link.

regional_links.note: The vaporetto network is entirely domestic within the Venetian Lagoon. There are no international legs — the whole proposal is domestic, inside sheltered lagoon water.

routing_hazards.instruction: Every domestic leg must be routed through navigable open water with NO land crossings (interior_land_km == 0). Hand-curated waypoints required wherever a breakwater, barrier, bridge pier, reef, headland, naval/exclusion zone or shallows would otherwise be clipped. Use data-clean/uae_hand_waypoints.json format {from, to, waypoints:[[lng,lat]...]}.

hazards.detail: Venice enforces strict speed and wake limits to protect building foundations, banks and the lagoon ecology; the Grand Canal and inner canals are no-foil, low-speed only — foiling is used only on the open lagoon crossings.
The Grand Canal and inner canals are crowded with vaporetti, water taxis, delivery boats and gondolas; conventional low-speed handling and strict give-way only.
The lagoon is shallow with mudflats (velme/barene) between marked channels staked by bricole; hand-waypoint the staked channels and never cut across the flats.
The MOSE storm-surge barriers close the lagoon inlets during high tides; routing must respect barrier-closure status and the acqua alta tidal range.
The Lido and Malamocco inlets open to the Adriatic with swell and current; manage exposure on the outer-edge legs.
The San Marco and Giudecca basins carry heavy public, commercial and (rerouted) large-vessel traffic; geofence speed and route clear of the working channels.
